claim_tested: For every N>=3 and every feasible endpoint h, the pair-length-three microfactorized Q bridge is connected under its two aligned H4 heat baths. A finite disconnected endpoint refutes this l=3 universal subclaim and the broader arbitrary-length base-connectivity proposition. Finite survival cannot prove either claim or a gap.
kernel_normalization: The nonlazy aligned chain chooses either H4 window with probability 1/2 and then samples uniformly from its exact same-product four-factor fiber. Connectivity uses only positive support.
quotient_lemma: At l=3, state components equal components of the bipartite graph on ordered first/last transposition pairs, with A--C iff prod(A)^(-1) h prod(C)^(-1) lies in supp(Q). Product copies have identical neighborhoods; the product-support quotient preserves components.
